name: Ro Khanna

lean.basis: Democratic congressman since 2017; co-chaired Bernie Sanders's 2020 campaign; calls himself a "progressive capitalist."

race_2028.basis: Frequent trips to New Hampshire and South Carolina and town halls in Republican districts; national outlets describe him as a potential 2028 contender, though he says he hasn't decided whether to run or back someone else.

current_role: U.S. representative for California's 17th district (Silicon Valley, since 2017)
summary: Ro Khanna, a Democratic congressman representing Silicon Valley since 2017, co-chaired Bernie Sanders's 2020 campaign while keeping ties to tech investors who backed his earlier runs. With Republican Thomas Massie he led the discharge petition that forced the House's 427–1 vote on November 18, 2025 to release the Epstein files, and he is discussed as a possible 2028 presidential candidate.

connections.name: Bernie Sanders
connections.description: Khanna endorsed Sanders in 2016 and co-chaired his 2020 presidential campaign.

connections.name: Barack Obama
connections.description: Obama appointed Khanna a deputy assistant secretary of Commerce (2009–2011); as a student Khanna had walked precincts in Obama's 1996 state senate race.

connections.name: Peter Thiel
connections.description: Thiel supported Khanna's congressional candidacies in 2011, 2013 and 2016.

connections.name: Nancy Pelosi
connections.description: Pelosi backed Khanna's 2014 House bid and in April 2018 asked him to draft an Internet Bill of Rights after the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

connections.name: Chuck Schumer
connections.description: Khanna, Schumer, Todd Young and Mike Gallagher co-wrote the Endless Frontier Act on technology research funding, a forerunner of the CHIPS and Science Act.

connections.name: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
connections.description: Khanna signed on to Ocasio-Cortez's Green New Deal proposal in 2018; both are prominent House progressives.

connections.name: Hakeem Jeffries
connections.description: Jeffries appointed Khanna to the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.

connections.name: Mike Honda
connections.description: Khanna lost to the incumbent Democrat Honda in 2014 and unseated him in 2016.

connections.name: Ron Klain
connections.description: Klain has been informally advising Khanna as he weighs a 2028 presidential run (Politico, June 2026).

sources.title: Ex-Biden honcho Ron Klain advising Ro Khanna as he mulls 2028 White House bid — Mediaite (citing Politico)

connections.name: Jamaal Bowman
connections.description: Bowman co-chairs Run Ro, a draft committee launched in November 2026 to urge Khanna to run for president.
